Definition: from G1537 and G218; to smear out, i.e. obliterate (erase tears, figuratively, pardon sin):--blot out, wipe away.
BiblicalUsage: exaleíphō means blot out, wipe away. In Acts 3:19, the text says "that your sins may be blotted out." In Colossians 2:14, the text says "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe exaleíphō shows us that forgiveness is real and it is free — because Someone else paid for it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Peter Preaches at Solomon's Porch; The Letter to the Church in Sardis; The Sealing of the 144,000
